waiting at N100 with part absent, air ok, two-hand released: the step records [0, 1, 0] and the client reads TC3's three labels with them
a part arriving turns record 1 on; two-hand still released holds N100
the slide sticks and times out extending: one MANUAL_RESET alarm sourced to the slide, dated today, blocking; the Unit's diagnostic is TC3's CYL_NOT_EXTENDED and names the slide's extended sensor
§8.3(b): START is refused, and its release report (TC3's) lists the unreset alarm beside the Unit's own fault; the refusal names the first
one operator reset: the event is closed into the ring with its gone time, nothing blocks, the Unit has no diagnostic - and, as TC3's OperatorReset releases its run command, the press is not running
the same START is accepted once nothing blocks
the ram failing at N200 is reported, not adopted: one closed AUTO_RESET ring entry sourced to the ram, nothing blocks, and the Unit's own diagnostic stays clear while the operator decides
a fresh AUTO session's rows are the clean path's steps, in the order they were first entered, on the controller and as published
the settle row records at least its declared delay; parked at N100 the cursor points at N100's row
within one mode session a re-run keeps its rows
MANUAL starts a new session: no rows, the epoch moved, nothing published
the ram failing at N200 marks N200's row as a warning, with a note naming the reason and the ram; no row is an error
re-entering N200 without a fault clears its mark and its note
TC3's FB_DigitalInputCM on the controller: Value follows the part stimulus both ways at good Quality, published as a digital input
held still by the fault injection, the slide times out extending: TC3's CYL_NOT_EXTENDED on the Unit, the slide and the alarm, naming _101B301A, after the declared 500 ms and not before
the ram held at N110: the Unit's own diagnostic is the ram's INTERLOCK_DROPPED (TC3 _M_RollupHold), no error, not timed out
TC3's SetAreaSafe: the door holds on INTERLOCK_DROPPED when air goes, does not time out or fault while held, the press reports it, and the stroke completes when air returns

TC3's N220: released part-way through the dwell, the dwell stands still on its named condition with no fault; past its expected time it is reported stalled; pressed again, the part is pressed for the declared dwell in total, not the dwell plus the pause
N100 waiting for a part: not timed out while it merely waits, then at StallTime timed out, with the Unit saying STEP_STALLED, LOW, no error
TC3's start latch: the part arriving after the two-hand press does not start the stroke - N100 still waits, nothing latched
a fresh press with the part there: the step moves, the stall and its diagnostic clear
START in MANUAL is refused by TC3's reason, manualHasNoAutoSequence, and nothing runs
TC3's catalogue on every cylinder: EXTEND 1 and RETRACT 2, with std.command labels; a sensor publishes none
a manual close with the slide outside is accepted and HELD on INTERLOCK_DROPPED, named doorCloseRequiresSlideInside, without moving and without timing out
a second command to the held door is refused as busy; OPERATOR_RESET drops the held command rather than resuming it
with the door closed (by a manual command, over the slide inside) the slide's way out is HELD, named slideOutsideRequiresDoorOpen; opening the door lets it finish without a fault
with the guard open the ram's press is HELD on pressRequiresGuardClosed; air lost as well, it names air - TC3's first-out order
a module that takes no commands, a command outside the catalogue, and any manual command outside MANUAL are each refused with its reason

TC3's Start consumes its release report: without air START is refused naming airPressureOk (PERMISSIVE_NOT_MET, the Unit's, an interlock) and answers with that report; with air back the report is released and START is taken
MANUAL, aborted and without air: three reasons in TC3's order - manualHasNoAutoSequence, unitNotReady, airPressureOk - not just the first
the door's close, asked about with the slide outside, is explained by doorCloseRequiresSlideInside (INTERLOCK_DROPPED, owned by Press.Door); its opening is released
TC3's ReleaseReportAction for ALARM_RESET with no blocking alarm: noBlockingAlarm
TC3's SupportedRunStylesPublished: all three offered, CONTINUOUS running
a style outside E_RunStyle: std.error.unsupportedRunStyleRequest, the style kept; a Step while stopped and a hold outside HOLD_TO_RUN refused by name; a release always taken
ST: nothing before the first Step, then exactly one command per Step - 8 for the cycle - and the cycle closes
SFC: nothing before the first Step, then exactly one command per Step - 8 for the cycle - and the cycle closes
LD: nothing before the first Step, then exactly one command per Step - 8 for the cycle - and the cycle closes

SFC: nothing unheld; released during the slide's motion the slide arrives and the door close waits un-issued; held again the cycle completes with its 8 commands
LD: nothing unheld; released during the slide's motion the slide arrives and the door close waits un-issued; held again the cycle completes with its 8 commands
held, then stopped: HoldRun is 0, and the next START in HOLD_TO_RUN issues nothing until held again
RESET_OEE is accepted: run and down zero, the ring empty, the epoch moved, and nothing valid yet (no run, no parts since)
one cycle and a wait at the start step: RunMs within 250 ms of the wall time from START to STOP, no down time, A and Q 1.0, and P = ideal x parts / run
the slide sticks: over a second in ERROR, DownMs grows by about that second and run and idle do not; A = run / (run + down)
the first sample lands 60 s after the reset (within a second), in the current epoch, holding the part made since and the model's ideal cycle, and the card shows it
RESET_OEE again: the ring is empty and its sample no longer valid; GoodCount is untouched, since counts reset only on their own logged action (Core §8.11.2)
TC3's classification, read where the HMI reads it: IDLE, CHANGEOVER selected, PRODUCING while running, STOPPED after STOP, IDLE after the reset, DOWN while faulted, IDLE once recovered
ReworkCount is published from the Unit's own counter; the press declares no rework verdict, so both read 0

one cycle after a START, read where the HMI reads it: the init step, the operator's start and the happy path in order; the total is its steps and the trend's; the two delays expected their recipe values and took one scan more; N100 is the only wait; N110 counted once more
STOP inside a cycle: the last cycle, its time and the trend are as they were (TC3's CycleAbandon), and the cycle is closed, not left open

the running model's baseline written to 300 ms: the first cycle's ~970 ms of WORK passes 360 and raises ONE CYCLE_TIME_DEGRADED (2007) occurrence, LOW, AUTO_RESET, from the Unit; the second, still degraded, raises none; the baseline is written back

TC3's pressAtLoadPosition: true at home, false the moment the slide goes in under a MANUAL command - no sequence runs to clear it - and true again when it comes out, each change stamped later than the last
TC3's pressTwoHandStartReady: armed, air and a part make it true; the part withdrawn makes it false at once, and back makes it true
